title: Regular Expression Matching
prompt:
Implement regex matching for `.` (any single char) and `*` (zero or more of the preceding element), matching the ENTIRE string `s` against pattern `p`.

**Example**: `s = "aab"`, `p = "c*a*b"` → `true`.

dp[i][j] = 'the first i chars of s match the first j chars of p'. The `*` is the tricky case: zero occurrences, or one-more when the preceding element matches.
hints: dp[0][0] = true. Seed dp[0][j] for patterns like `a*b*` that can match the empty string.
For `x*`: dp[i][j] = dp[i][j-2] (zero of x), OR (x matches s[i-1] AND dp[i-1][j]) (consume one more).
For a normal char or `.`: dp[i][j] = dp[i-1][j-1] when it matches s[i-1].

solution.explanation: `x*` has two meanings: erase it (dp[i][j-2]) or, if `x` matches the current char, absorb that char and stay on the same `*` (dp[i-1][j]) — this is what lets `a*` match any run of a's. Plain chars and `.` advance both indices on a match. The empty-string seeding handles patterns that are entirely erasable. O(m·n).
